rationale: C03 supplies the child’s core drafting structure and much of its precise language: the same enumerated classes of tax returns, the same open-to-inspection authorization, a changed Senate committee and investigative purpose, the same Treasury-decision condition, and an updated terminal period from 1949 to 1950. C17 is another close inspection-order template and likely contributed the effective-date clause, but its narrower return-selection machinery is less directly matched. C22 shares the inspection mechanism and effective-date formula but is materially less similar.

shared_material.child_excerpt: any income, excess-profits, declared value excess-profits, capital stock, estate, or gift tax return for any period to and including 1950 shall be open to inspection
shared_material.parent_excerpt: any income, excess profits, declared value excess-profits, capital stock, estate, and gift tax returns for any period to and including 1949 shall be open to inspection
shared_material.explanation: Near-verbatim operative authorization with the cutoff year updated from 1949 to 1950.

shared_material.child_excerpt: by the Senate Committee on Armed Services or any duly authorized subcommittee thereof for the purpose of exercising a continuous watchfulness
shared_material.parent_excerpt: by the Special Committee established pursuant to Senate Resolution 202 ... for the purpose of carrying out the provisions of the said Senate Resolution
shared_material.explanation: The same committee-inspection and stated-purpose slots are retained while the committee and mandate are replaced.

shared_material.child_excerpt: subject to the conditions stated in the Treasury decision relating to the inspection of such returns by that committee, approved by me this date
shared_material.parent_excerpt: subject to the conditions stated in the Treasury decision relating to the inspection of such returns by that Committee, approved by me this date
shared_material.explanation: Distinctive administrative condition is reproduced essentially verbatim.
